target_customer: Retail traders and crypto and prediction market users who want automated strategies without coding
problem: Turning a market view into a tested, automated strategy requires coding and backtesting skills most retail traders lack.
business_model: Consumer trading automation platform, pricing not verified; trades through connected brokers

founders.name: Aria Vikram
founders.background_notes: YC page also lists Google Code-In Grand Prize, RSI alum and USAID awardee; education not listed

founders.name: Tony Yamin
prior_employers: Booz Allen (ML infrastructure for the U.S. Department of Defense)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists hackathon wins at HackPrinceton and YaleHack

competitors.name: Stralgo
competitors.what: AI backtesting agent where traders describe strategies in plain English

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM to strategy translation, backtesting and broker integrations are standard engineering, but reliable live execution across asset classes adds hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Prompt to strategy pipelines are easy to copy; brokers and APIs are shared. Possible edge from community strategies and user data, not shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The site integrates with Robinhood and Alpaca as execution brokers; no evidence of copying found.

market_need_then: Retail interest in algorithmic and crypto trading and rising LLM capability in 2025; no quantified demand source found.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with a VC firm and other firms, which blurs search results; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Conviction is active as of November 2026 with a three person team and no verified funding round. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff reports were found. The space has several similar plain English trading tools and brokers as distribution partners, so the outcome is undetermined and depends on whether it builds a user base beyond the early adopters.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125K seed with no investors and no second source; unverified so no round recorded. Search results for Conviction mostly describe unrelated firms (the VC firm, Convictional).
